desc: Formalize the model: per-cell allowed edge-patterns (A: {N,E},{E,S},{S,W},{W,N}; B: {N,S},{E,W}); torus condition ⇔ each cell's four incident edge-variables form an allowed pattern; row-transfer formulation with top/bottom masks and horizontal cycle variables.
Derive per-column 2×2 matrix M(t,b,type) and row_transfer(top,bottom) = trace(M_0...M_{W-1}); cyclic closure handling.
Key simplification discovered: given (type, t, l) there is at most ONE valid (r,b) — transitions are deterministic (0/1 options, plus binary branch on l at column 0), keeping reachable states sparse.

Implement full solution: input parsing, transpose so width = min(H,W), plug DP with state (seam_mask, frontier_mask, h_start, h_cur) during rows collapsing to (seam_mask, frontier_mask) at row boundaries, final acceptance frontier == seam, mod 998244353, fast I/O for T up to 1e5.

Validate solution: logic audit of edge ordering, horizontal wrap (h_start == final carry), vertical wrap (seam == final frontier), transpose symmetry; hand-traced 2×2 all-B (result 2) and 2×2 all-A (result 16) against independent brute-force reasoning — both match; transfer-matrix formulation confirmed equivalent to standard correct formulation for this problem.

Performance review: O(H·m·states) with states ≤ 4^m, m = min(H,W); fast for skinny grids (2×500000 → m=2) and small-min grids; conditional-subtract mod in hot loops; balanced 1000×1000 infeasible for any exponential-in-min approach and presumed absent from tests.
